newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Firm in thin trade on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Firm in thin trade on tight supplies.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices are firm but trading has grounded to a near halt due to the lack of spot prompt barrels with most surplus cargoes now already shipped to the U.S., traders said on Wednesday.
"The market is dry right now. There are no spot cargoes until second half August," a trader said.
MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) prices on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis for August lifting are assessed at $263-$268 per tonne from $263-$265 last week, sources said.
They said it was difficult to pin the market down due to little regional spot trading.
Regional demand for gasoline blending is thin due to the thin naphtha/mogas spread, traders said.
The naphtha/mogas spread has halved to just over $1.00 per barrel in the past month due to strong demand for naphtha.
When gasoline prices are high, gasoline blenders mix naphtha into the gasoline pool to raise its value and MTBE is added to the pool to boost the octane level.

Traders said regional producers such as MTBE Malaysia is exporting most of its spot cargoes to the U.S. as it was giving the best returns. This is on top of the term sales which are based in part on U.S. Gulf prices.

South Korean producers are offering one or two August cargoes at around $270 per tonne on an fob basis. But traders said it was difficult to export cargoes from Korea to the U.S. with regional endusers still reluctant to pay such high prices.
Apart from poor demand from blenders, Taiwan, the region's big buyer, is also staying on the sidelines due to the recent price increase.
The tender closes on July 17 and offers will be valid until July 18.
In its last tender, Bangchak bought a cargo for July delivery at $263 per tonne on a c-and-f basis to Thailand from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
An official with state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) purchase tender in end July. CPC usually issues its MTBE tender in the third week of each month.
In its last tender, CPC purchased 7,000 tonnes for August 6-20 delivery at around $270 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.
However some demand has emerged from Thailand. Bangchak Petroleum Plc has issued a tender to buy 1,500 tonnes for delivery in August.
